candidates.change_summary: Remove the assignment to number so it keeps its previous value after setL1BlockValues.
Change the assignment to number so it stores _timestamp instead of _number.
Change the assignment to number so it stores _basefee (cast to uint64) instead of _number.
Change the assignment to number so it stores _sequenceNumber instead of _number.
Remove the onlyDepositor modifier so anyone can call setL1BlockValues and change number.
Replace `timestamp = _timestamp;` with `timestamp = _number;` causing timestamp to get the wrong input value.
Replace `timestamp = _timestamp;` with `timestamp = uint64(_basefee);` causing timestamp to be set from a different argument after truncation.
Delete `timestamp = _timestamp;` so timestamp remains at its previous or default value after the call.

Move `timestamp = _timestamp;` after `number = _number;` to after the `l1FeeScalar` assignment so it is overwritten by an intervening assignment to `timestamp` (none exist, but reordering could later interact if another statement writes to timestamp; here this move alone does not change behavior because no other write to timestamp exists, so this is NOT a valid mutant — actually, moving it doesn't change semantics. A valid move would swap it with another assignment that also writes to timestamp, but there is none. Ignore move for this reason.)
Remove the `onlyDepositor` modifier from `setL1BlockValues` so any caller can change `timestamp` to an arbitrary value.
Replace `require(msg.sender == DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT, ...)` with `require(msg.sender == address(this), ...)` so the depositor can no longer call, but the contract itself can.
Replace `basefee = _basefee;` with `basefee = _basefee + 1;` so that the stored value differs by exactly one.
Delete the line `basefee = _basefee;` so that `basefee` retains its previous value and does not change to `_basefee`.
Replace `basefee = _basefee;` with `basefee = 0;` so the stored value is always zero instead of the argument value.
Delete the assignment to hash so it retains the default zero value instead of being updated.
Replace the right-hand side of the hash assignment with a constant bytes32 zero value.
Replace the right-hand side of the hash assignment with a different parameter, e.g. _batcherHash.
Replace the right-hand side of the hash assignment with a different parameter, e.g. keccak256(abi.encodePacked(_hash)).
Remove the onlyDepositor modifier from setL1BlockValues so anyone can call it and change hash.
Replace the assignment `sequenceNumber = _sequenceNumber;` with `sequenceNumber = _sequenceNumber + 1;` so that the stored sequence number always differs from the input argument.
Replace the assignment `sequenceNumber = _sequenceNumber;` with `sequenceNumber = 0;` so that the stored sequence number is always zero regardless of the input.
Delete the assignment `sequenceNumber = _sequenceNumber;` so the state variable `sequenceNumber` remains unchanged after the call.
Replace the assignment `sequenceNumber = _sequenceNumber;` with `sequenceNumber = _number;` so sequenceNumber is set from a different input parameter.
Delete the `onlyDepositor` modifier from the function signature so anyone can call setL1BlockValues and change sequenceNumber.
